On a local domain their differences define rational-function orders. For a finite extension of such domains, the order of a field norm is the sum of upstairs orders weighted by residue-field degrees.
thm-author-1437578267d2-curve-norm-input.hypotheses: For orders: a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with the stated fraction field and nonzero numerator and denominator. For the norm formula: a finite domain extension of this local domain and a nonzero element of its fraction field. No normality or separability assumption.
thm-author-1437578267d2-curve-norm-input.reading_limits: Read the indicated definition, both lemma statements and their displayed proofs, as well as the separate 02MD and 02MJ pages. Checked that the length convention matches the singular-curve formula below. Linked finite-length, semilocal and determinant-length prerequisites are accepted through these external results, not reconstructed locally.

thm-author-1437578267d2-curve-norm-input.title: The Stacks Project, Weil divisors
thm-author-1437578267d2-curve-norm-input.statement: On a locally Noetherian integral scheme, orders at prime divisors use the one-dimensional local-ring length convention. Nonzero orders of a rational function have locally finite support, giving its principal Weil divisor and an additive divisor map. On a quasi-compact scheme this support is finite.
thm-author-1437578267d2-curve-norm-input.hypotheses: The scheme is integral and locally Noetherian; the rational function is nonzero. Quasi-compactness is used for finite support. For curves, prime divisors are reduced closed points. Normality is not required.
thm-author-1437578267d2-curve-norm-input.reading_limits: Read the listed definitions, lemma statements and displayed proofs in the section, including the finite-sum convention in its introduction. Also read the separate 02RJ and 02RL pages. Checked the quasi-compact curve specialization. Deeper linked results on local rings, codimension and Noetherian spaces were not reconstructed.

thm-author-1437578267d2-curve-norm-input.statement: For an irreducible closed subset of a scheme with generic point xi, its codimension equals the dimension of the local ring at xi.
thm-author-1437578267d2-curve-norm-input.hypotheses: A scheme, an irreducible closed subset and its generic point. A reduced closed point in an integral scheme of chain dimension one has codimension one, so its local ring has dimension one.
thm-author-1437578267d2-curve-norm-input.reading_limits: Read the complete lemma statement and displayed proof. Checked the closed-point specialization on an integral curve. The linked affine and topological codimension lemmas were not reconstructed.

thm-author-1437578267d2-curve-norm-input.title: The Stacks Project, Field-base dimension comparison

Thus the two curves have delta-dimension one and reduced closed points have delta-dimension zero.

thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.title: Jacob Lurie, Higher Algebra (September 18, 2017): spectrum objects, tower and pointed adjunction
thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.locator: Definition 1.4.2.8 (p. 142); Corollary 1.4.2.17, Remark 1.4.2.18 and Notation 1.4.2.20 (p. 146); Proposition 1.4.2.24 and Remark 1.4.2.25 (p. 147); Definition 1.4.3.1 and Remark 1.4.3.3 (p. 150); Proposition 1.4.4.4, especially proof assertion (2′) (pp. 156–157), and sphere definition immediately before Corollary 1.4.4.6 (p. 157)
thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.statement: Reduced excisive functors from finite pointed spaces to spaces form a stable presentable infinity-category. Stabilization is unchanged by passing from the target to its pointed objects; for a pointed target with finite limits, it is the homotopy limit of its loop tower. Evaluation at the pointed zero-sphere has a pointed lift with a left adjoint on pointed objects when the target is presentable. For spaces its left adjoint sends the pointed zero-sphere to the sphere spectrum; the nth tower projection is evaluation on the nth sphere, equivalently evaluation after the nth suspension shift.
thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.hypotheses: The spectrum-object construction uses a target with finite limits. The tower theorem is applied to pointed spaces; Remark 1.4.2.18 identifies its stabilization with that of spaces. Presentability is required for Proposition 1.4.4.4. Spaces are presentable by reference 2 below. All smallness is relative to the stated universes and the imported results are used in their classical set-theoretic setting.

thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.title: Jacob Lurie, Higher Topos Theory: infinity-categories, spaces, diagrams and coherent structures
thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.locator: Definition 1.1.2.4 and Example 1.1.2.6 (p. 14); Definitions 1.1.5.1 and 1.1.5.5 (pp. 20–22); right mapping-space construction and Proposition 1.2.2.3 (p. 27); Notation 1.2.7.2 and Proposition 1.2.7.3 (p. 39); Definition 1.2.13.4 and Remark 1.2.13.5 (p. 47); Definition 1.2.16.1 (p. 51); Definition 2.4.2.1 (p. 121); Proposition 2.4.4.3 (pp. 131–132), used dually; Definition 3.0.0.1 (p. 144); Definition 5.2.2.7 and Proposition 5.2.2.8 (pp. 342–343)
thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.statement: Use quasicategories (inner-horn-filling simplicial sets), their right mapping Kan complexes and internal-hom functor infinity-categories. Spaces are the simplicial nerve of the simplicial category of Kan complexes. Limits and colimits are terminal cones and initial cocones, respectively. The infinity-category of infinity-categories uses the cores of functor categories as mapping spaces. CoCartesian fibrations are the dual of Cartesian fibrations, with their edges characterized by the dual mapping-space pullback criterion. An adjunction is characterized by a unit inducing the mapping-space equivalences.
thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.hypotheses: Use simplicial sets in the stated size universes. The functor-category assertion requires an infinity-category as target. The coCartesian mapping-space criterion applies to an inner fibration between infinity-categories; the monoidal base is the nerve of the category of finite pointed sets. The unit criterion concerns functors between infinity-categories.

thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.title: Jacob Lurie, Higher Topos Theory: accessibility, presentability and completeness
thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.locator: Definition 5.3.1.7 (p. 382); Definition 5.3.4.5 (p. 396); Definition 5.4.2.1 and Proposition 5.4.2.2 (pp. 423–424); Definition 5.5.0.1 (p. 456); Example 5.5.1.8 (p. 461); Corollary 5.5.2.4 (p. 464)
thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.statement: For a regular cardinal kappa, kappa-filtered indexing infinity-categories admit cocones for every kappa-small simplicial diagram; kappa-compact objects corepresent functors preserving those colimits. An infinity-category admitting small kappa-filtered colimits and generated under them by an essentially small full subcategory of kappa-compact objects is accessible. Presentable means accessible and admitting small colimits. Spaces are presentable, and every presentable infinity-category admits all small limits.
thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.hypotheses: Kappa is an infinite regular cardinal in the small universe. Compactness is defined for categories admitting the relevant filtered colimits. In the characterization of accessibility use Proposition 5.4.2.2(3), including generation by a full essentially small subcategory of compact objects. Completeness requires presentability.
thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.reading_limits: In this repair, read the specified definitions, Proposition 5.4.2.2(3), Example 5.5.1.8 and Corollary 5.5.2.4. Their proofs and the general Ind-completion theory are imported, not reconstructed. Only their application to spaces and spectra is used.

thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.title: Jacob Lurie, Higher Algebra (September 18, 2017): finite spaces, stability and symmetric monoidal smash
thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.locator: Proposition 1.1.3.4 (p. 31); Definition 1.4.2.1 and Notation 1.4.2.5 (p. 141); Corollary 1.4.2.27 (pp. 149–150); Definition 2.0.0.7 (p. 169); Corollary 4.8.2.19 and following characterization (pp. 722–723)
thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.statement: Finite spaces are the full subcategory generated by the point under finite colimits, with finite pointed spaces its pointed objects. Reduced means preserving the final object and excisive means sending pushout squares to pullback squares. Stability is equivalent to pointedness, existence of finite limits and colimits, and coincidence of pullback and pushout squares. A symmetric monoidal infinity-category is a coCartesian fibration over the nerve of finite pointed sets with product (Segal) fibers. Spectra admit such a structure with sphere unit and tensor product preserving small colimits separately in each variable; this is the smash product.
thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.hypotheses: Use the finite-colimit closure of the point as the domain for spectrum objects. The stability criterion assumes a pointed infinity-category. The Segal equivalences are induced by the maps selecting each non-basepoint element. The first existence assertion of Corollary 4.8.2.19 is applied to spectra; its subsequent universal property for other stable presentable monoidal categories is not asserted here.
thm-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-stable-enhanceme.reading_limits: In this repair, read the listed definitions and propositions, including the whole statement and following two-property characterization of Corollary 4.8.2.19. The existence proof of the smash structure and the general tensor product of presentable infinity-categories are imported. No claim of reading all of Chapter 4 or of independent acceptance is made.

lem-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-omega-tower-shif.statement: The based loop Kan complex is the fiber of a Kan fibration from a contractible path complex to the pointed Kan complex. Its homotopy groups identify with those of the original complex one degree higher.
lem-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-omega-tower-shif.hypotheses: A pointed Kan complex, with the constant loop as base point; nonnegative homotopy degree. The long exact sequence is applied to the displayed Kan fibration.

lem-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-omega-tower-shif.title: Jacob Lurie, Higher Algebra (September 18, 2017), suspension and mapping-space groups
lem-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-omega-tower-shif.locator: Construction preceding Notation 1.1.2.7 and Remark 1.1.2.8, printed pp. 23–24 (PDF pages 23–24); Notation 1.4.2.5, printed p. 141 (PDF page 141)

Double suspension gives abelian component groups; in a stable infinity-category these groups are functorial in both variables. Pointed spheres are objects of pointed spaces.
lem-author-e0b0bf18ed2b-omega-tower-shif.hypotheses: A pointed infinity-category with the indicated fibers and cofibers; invertible suspension for the stable mapping-group assertion. Applied to pointed spaces and to the stable category of spectra supplied by the declared enhancement.

thm-author-4f716d60801a-derived-enhancem.title: Jacob Lurie, Higher Algebra, September 18, 2017
thm-author-4f716d60801a-derived-enhancem.statement: Derived localization is stable, presentable and reflective from the dg nerve of complexes. The fibrant model is K-injective and its homotopy maps are maps modulo homotopy. Cones are dg cofibers. Localization has the functor-category universal property. Stable functors preserving zero and cofiber sequences are exact; stable idempotent completeness is equivalent to that of the homotopy category.
thm-author-4f716d60801a-derived-enhancem.hypotheses: Grothendieck abelian categories for the unbounded derived construction; an additive category for the dg cone assertion; stable infinity-categories for the exactness and idempotent-completeness criteria. Use larger universes for categories of complexes. Reverse homological grading to the stated cochain convention.
thm-author-4f716d60801a-derived-enhancem.reading_limits: Inspected the listed statements, the displayed cone argument, the localization discussion and proofs of 1.3.5.13–15, and the proof of 1.3.5.21(1). thm-author-4f716d60801a-derived-enhancem.locator: Definitions 4.4.5.2 and 4.4.5.4 (p. 304); Corollary 4.4.5.15, Proposition 4.4.5.17 and Remark 4.4.5.18 (p. 308); Definition 5.5.0.1 (p. 456)

thm-author-4f716d60801a-local-perfect-in.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves, Perfect complexes
thm-author-4f716d60801a-local-perfect-in.statement: Perfect objects are locally represented by strictly perfect complexes; every representative is locally perfect as a complex. With local stalk rings, bounded finite locally free local models are equivalent. Perfection is invariant and local, satisfies two-out-of-three in distinguished triangles, and passes to direct summands.
thm-author-4f716d60801a-local-perfect-in.hypotheses: A ringed space and objects of its module-sheaf derived category; local stalk rings only for the finite locally free characterization. No quasi-compactness or uniform global bound is assumed.

thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-kflat-.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves, Flat resolutions
thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-kflat-.locator: Section 20.26: Lemmas 20.26.1, 20.26.3–6, 20.26.8–13 and 20.26.17; Definitions 20.26.2 and 20.26.14 and the discussion preceding 20.26.14; its sign convention is Section 15.74 (0FNG), opening rules (6) and (9).
thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-kflat-.statement: Unbounded complexes of structure-sheaf modules have K-flat resolutions with flat terms. The K-flat test is stalkwise and stable under shifts, cones and total tensor. Tensor with a K-flat complex preserves quasi-isomorphisms; tensor with any complex preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes. K-flat replacement defines derived tensor, with the Koszul signed symmetry.
thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-kflat-.hypotheses: An arbitrary ringed space with commutative structure sheaf; all complexes are complexes of its module sheaves and all tensor products use that structure sheaf. Direct-sum totalization has the cochain Koszul differential. AC and the stated universe convention are retained for the imported resolution machinery; no geometric finiteness assumption.

thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-enhanc.title: Blumberg–Gepner–Tabuada, Uniqueness of the multiplicative cyclotomic trace

thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-enhanc.title: Jacob Lurie, Higher Algebra
thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-enhanc.locator: Definitions 1.1.1.9 and 1.3.1.1; Construction 1.3.1.6; Proposition 1.3.2.10, Remark 1.3.2.17 and paragraph following its proof (pp. 89–92); Proposition 1.3.4.5 (p. 109); Proposition 1.3.5.15 (p. 127); Definitions 2.0.0.7, 2.1.1.8 and 2.1.2.1

thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-enhanc.title: Brad Drew, Verdier quotients of stable quasi-categories are localizations
thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-enhanc.locator: Definition 1.1 and Theorem 1.3, printed pp. 5–6 (PDF pp. 6–7)
thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-enhanc.statement: If A is a stable full subcategory of a small stable infinity-category C, then localization of C at maps whose cofibers lie in A is the stable Verdier quotient C/A. In particular that ordinary infinity-localization is stable.

thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-enhanc.title: Vladimir Hinich, Dwyer–Kan localization revisited
thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-enhanc.locator: §1.1.2–1.1.3; Definition 2.1.1, Proposition 2.1.4 and complete proof §2.1.5–2.2.6; Definition 3.2.1 and Proposition 3.2.2; PDF pp. 4–5, 16–22
thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-enhanc.statement: Localization is an actual functor L:Cat_∞^+→Cat_∞ with a natural localization map. A marked cocartesian fibration localizes to a cocartesian fibration with the localized fibers (Proposition 2.1.4). Tensor-stable markings give a symmetric monoidal localization with the full symmetric monoidal functor universal property (Proposition 3.2.2).
thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-enhanc.hypotheses: Definition 2.1.1 requires a cocartesian fibration, marked cocartesian lifts of marked base edges, preservation of fiber markings by every transport, and equivalence of localized fibers over marked base edges. Markings are saturated. For symmetric monoidal localization every active Fin_* transport must preserve the markings. Use equivalences as base markings, componentwise quasi-isomorphisms in the fibers, and all categories in a sufficiently large universe.

lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kflat-addendum-l.title: Jacob Lurie, Higher Algebra (September 18, 2017)
lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kflat-addendum-l.locator: Section 1.1.2, suspension/loop construction and mapping-space discussion preceding Lemma 1.1.2.9, printed p. 24 (zero-based PDF index 23); Notation 1.1.2.17, p. 30 (index 29); Proposition 1.1.4.1, pp. 33–34 (indices 32–33).
lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kflat-addendum-l.statement: In a stable infinity-category suspension and loop are inverse. Suspension in the source identifies the mapping space with the based loop of the unshifted mapping space; iterating identifies positive homotopy groups at zero with shifted homotopy-category Hom groups. A functor between stable infinity-categories is exact precisely when it preserves zero and cofiber sequences, equivalently finite limits or finite colimits.
lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kflat-addendum-l.hypotheses: Stable infinity-categories in fixed universes, mapping spaces pointed by the zero morphism; shifts are suspension powers. The exactness criterion requires both source and target stable. No presentability, field or K-projectivity hypothesis is imposed.
lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kflat-addendum-l.reading_limits: This adjudication read the PDF text of the suspension/loop construction and mapping-space discussion on printed p. 24, Notation 1.1.2.17, and Proposition 1.1.4.1 with its displayed proof. lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kflat-addendum-l.statement: A weak homotopy equivalence is bijective on components and isomorphic on every positive based homotopy group. Spaces are used up to weak homotopy equivalence, equivalently in the simplicial or topological model. An infinity-functor is fully faithful when its maps of mapping spaces are equivalences; it is an equivalence if it is fully faithful and essentially surjective on the ordinary homotopy category.

The four marked-cocartesian conditions are those listed explicitly in [F8]. Coc(D), with cocartesian-preserving morphisms, is equivalent to Fun(D,Cat∞). The marked family localizes over L(D,W); its classifying functor extends L∘F⁺, and its pullback to D is classified by L∘F⁺. Componentwise markings preserved by all active transports permit strict symmetric monoidal localization.

Cocartesian fibrations in Cat∞ are understood up to the presentations in Definition 2.1.3.

The representability theorem concerns nonconnective IK.

lem-author-3a003d7b5208-triangle-present.title: Jacob Lurie, Higher Algebra (September 18, 2017): stability and cofibers
lem-author-3a003d7b5208-triangle-present.locator: Definition 0.0.0.1, printed p. 11; Definitions 1.1.1.1, 1.1.1.4 and 1.1.1.6, Remarks 1.1.1.5 and 1.1.1.7, Definition 1.1.1.9, printed pp. 17–20; Proposition 1.1.3.4, printed p. 31.
lem-author-3a003d7b5208-triangle-present.statement: Use the inner-horn definition of infinity-category. A zero object is both initial and final; a cofiber sequence is a pushout square with a zero lower-left vertex. Cofibers, when they exist, are unique up to equivalence. Stability is equivalent to being pointed, admitting finite limits and colimits, and having exactly the same pushout and pullback squares.
lem-author-3a003d7b5208-triangle-present.hypotheses: For cofibers, a pointed infinity-category and the indicated pushout; for the stability characterization, a pointed infinity-category. The item assumes a small stable infinity-category, so the required finite colimits exist.

lem-author-3a003d7b5208-triangle-present.locator: Suspension construction preceding Notation 1.1.2.7, printed pp. 23–24; Definition 1.1.2.11, printed p. 26; Theorem 1.1.2.14 and Remark 1.1.2.15, printed p. 27.
lem-author-3a003d7b5208-triangle-present.statement: Suspension is the pushout of the two zero maps from X, is invertible in a stable infinity-category, and induces translation on the homotopy category. Distinguished triangles are the diagrams obtained from two coherent adjacent pushout squares with zero objects at the lower-left and upper-right corners. A pointed infinity-category with cofibers and invertible suspension has the resulting triangulated homotopy category; every stable infinity-category meets these hypotheses.
lem-author-3a003d7b5208-triangle-present.hypotheses: The theorem assumes pointedness, existence of cofibers, and equivalence of the suspension functor. Remark 1.1.2.15 applies it to every stable infinity-category. Smallness is needed only for the present group presentations, not for this theorem.

lem-author-3a003d7b5208-triangle-present.title: Jacob Lurie, Higher Topos Theory: homotopy categories, equivalences and limits
lem-author-3a003d7b5208-triangle-present.locator: Definition 1.1.5.14, printed p. 25; Definition 1.2.2.1 and Proposition 1.2.2.3, printed pp. 26–27; Section 1.2.3, Propositions 1.2.3.5 and 1.2.3.9, printed pp. 30–33; Section 1.2.4, opening paragraphs, printed p. 33; Definition 1.2.13.4 and Remark 1.2.13.5, printed p. 47.
lem-author-3a003d7b5208-triangle-present.statement: Mapping spaces are the homotopy types of morphisms in the enriched homotopy category, as in Definition 1.2.2.1. The homotopy category has the same objects and homotopy classes of edges as morphisms; every morphism is represented by an edge. An edge is an equivalence precisely when its image is an isomorphism in the homotopy category. Limits and colimits are final and initial coherent cones respectively, with colimits determined up to a contractible space of choices.
lem-author-3a003d7b5208-triangle-present.hypotheses: An infinity-category (a quasicategory), two objects for the mapping-space assertion, and a specified simplicial diagram for the limit/colimit definition. No stability hypothesis is needed for these facts.

thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-.title: Algebraic K-theory of stable ∞-categories via binary complexes

thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-.statement: Infinity-categories are simplicial sets with inner-horn fillers. An idempotent completion is fully faithful into an idempotent-complete category whose objects are retracts of image objects, and it exists.

lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-quotient-.title: The Stacks Project, Quotients of triangulated categories
lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-quotient-.statement: For a full triangulated subcategory A of a triangulated category C, maps with cone in A form a two-sided multiplicative system. The Verdier quotient C/A is its localization, with an exact quotient functor. An exact functor annihilating A factors through it as an exact functor.
lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-quotient-.hypotheses: C is triangulated and A is a full triangulated subcategory with inherited triangles. Apply to the ordinary homotopy categories of perfect complexes and the full supported subcategory. Use the supplied small equivalent models when invoking the library calculus-of-fractions theorem; no local-smallness-only assertion is used.

thm-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-tt-extens.title: R. W. Thomason and Thomas Trobaugh, Higher Algebraic K-Theory of Schemes and of Derived Categories
thm-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-tt-extens.locator: §5, hypotheses of Theorem 5.1 p. 337; Propositions 5.2.2–5.2.4 pp. 338–339; general-qcqs completion Lemma 5.6.2 and 5.6.3 pp. 348–350; Euler relations 1.5.6–1.5.7 p. 261. PDF pages 91–93, 102–104 and 15.
thm-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-tt-extens.statement: For qcqs X and quasi-compact open j:U→X, restriction of ordinary perfect derived categories has the following properties: every morphism between restricted objects admits a roof on X whose denominator becomes invertible on U; two morphisms equal on U become equal after such a denominator; a perfect F on U extends exactly when its Euler class is in the image of restriction. In particular F⊕F[1] extends because its Euler class is zero.
thm-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-tt-extens.hypotheses: X quasi-compact and quasi-separated, U a quasi-compact open. These are the unrestrained-support clauses 5.2.2(a), 5.2.3(a), 5.2.4(a); set the additional Z of 5.1 equal to X. No ample-family, noetherian, regularity or resolution-property assumption survives 5.6.3.

thm-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-categoric.title: Andrew J. Blumberg, David Gepner and Gonçalo Tabuada, A universal characterization of higher algebraic K-theory
thm-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-categoric.locator: Introduction p. 4; §2.2, Definition 2.12, following homotopy-category paragraph and idempotent-completion paragraph, p. 14; §5.1, cofiber convention following Definition 5.12 and Proposition 5.13, p. 35; Propositions 5.14–5.15, pp. 35–36; Definition 8.1, p. 52; Theorem 8.7, p. 55; Definition 9.6 and Theorem 9.8, p. 58.
thm-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-categoric.statement: The category Cat_ex consists of small stable infinity-categories and exact functors. Idem is left adjoint to the inclusion of Cat_perf. The cofiber quotient of a fully faithful exact functor exists in Cat_ex; its homotopy category agrees with the triangulated Verdier quotient. Exactness is equivalent to equivalence of the induced quotient functor after idempotent completion, and is detected on the triangulated sequence. On all of Cat_ex, U_loc inverts Morita equivalences and sends exact sequences to cofiber sequences. Its spectral mapping functor from U_loc(Sp^omega) is naturally BGT nonconnective IK.
thm-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-categoric.hypotheses: Compatible fixed universes, ZFC/AC conventions, small stable infinity-categories and actual exact functors. In §5 specialize kappa=omega, so the required colimits are finite; quotient equivalence is after idempotent completion. Supply the nullhomotopy of the composite to specify the induced quotient map. The kappa=omega specialization concerns the §5 criterion only, not the auxiliary cardinal in the construction of §9. Essentially small categories are handled through the equivalent domain of small presentations.

thm-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-categoric.statement: For a full triangulated subcategory N of a triangulated category T, the arrows with a cone isomorphic to an object of N form a multiplicative system compatible with triangles. thm-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-classic.title: Charles Weibel, The K-book, Chapter IV
thm-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-classic.statement: For small exact E, Quillen K^Q(E) is the based loop space of BQ(E), where Q morphisms are isomorphism classes of admissible epimorphism/monomorphism spans composed by pullback. For small Waldhausen D, K^W(D) is the loop space of the realization of the nerves of wS_n(D). The canonical matrix, group-completion, Q and exact-category S comparisons agree on automorphism classes. For finite projectives these identify GL(A)_ab with pi_1 K^Q(P(A)); the canonical S/Q equivalence matches the same automorphisms. Essentially small exact categories are handled by a small equivalent category.
thm-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-classic.hypotheses: Unital rings; the application restricts to commutative rings. P(A) is split exact. Its small idempotent-matrix presentation represents all finite projectives. Stabilization is diag(M,1). The S/Q comparison applies to small exact categories, with isomorphisms as weak equivalences. Matrix-loop orientation is fixed by eta_n(g)=(g,1), Exercise IV.7.9(c) and Exercise IV.8.7, reading the last exercise’s cross-reference as IV.7.9.

thm-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-classic.locator: Theorem V.2.2 (Gillet–Waldhausen) and proof, pp. 13–14; §V.2.7.2, p. 18
thm-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-classic.statement: For an exact category closed under kernels of surjections in an ambient abelian category, inclusion as complexes concentrated in degree zero induces a K-theory equivalence with its bounded chain-complex Waldhausen category. In particular K(P(A))≃K(Chᵇ(P(A))).
thm-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-classic.hypotheses: P(A) is the category of finite projective A-modules, with split exact sequences. Chᵇ(P(A)) has degreewise split monomorphisms as cofibrations and quasi-isomorphisms as weak equivalences; the ambient abelian category is all A-modules. Kernels of surjections between finite projectives are finite projective because the sequence splits. Cochain reindexing does not change the statement.

lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-c.title: Elden Elmanto and Matthew Morrow, Motivic cohomology of equicharacteristic schemes, arXiv:2309.08463v1

thm-author-dcdf962edbda-source-input.statement: Weight-zero natural pullback squares in D(Z): the top-left and bottom-left objects are Z(0)_mot(X) and Z(0)_cdh(X). Over Q the right column is RΓ(X, Hodge-completed derived de Rham over Q) → RΓ_cdh(X, Hodge-completed derived de Rham over Q). Over F_p it is Z_p(0)_syn(X) → (L_cdh Z_p(0)_syn)(X). thm-adjudicate-1ef158934564-ringed-deriv.title: Jacob Lurie, Higher Algebra: localization, differential graded nerves, and cofibers
thm-adjudicate-1ef158934564-ringed-deriv.locator: Definition 1.1.1.9; §1.1.4 opening and Proposition 1.1.4.1; Definition 1.3.1.1, Construction 1.3.1.6, Remarks 1.3.1.9 and 1.3.1.11, and functoriality discussion 1.3.1.18–20; Definition 1.3.2.1 and Remark 1.3.2.2; Remark 1.3.2.17; Definition 1.3.4.1
thm-adjudicate-1ef158934564-ringed-deriv.statement: Localization is universal on full functor infinity-categories, including natural transformations. Differential graded functors induce functors of differential graded nerves; in the nerve of complexes, edges are chain maps and their homotopies are chain homotopies. The canonical mapping-cone square is a cofiber square. A stable infinity-category has a zero object and fibers and cofibers with coincident fiber and cofiber sequences; preserving zero objects and cofiber sequences is the exactness condition, equivalently preservation of finite limits and finite colimits.
thm-adjudicate-1ef158934564-ringed-deriv.hypotheses: For localization, an infinity-category and a collection of edges, with larger universes as necessary. For complexes, an additive category; for exactness, source and target stable infinity-categories.
thm-adjudicate-1ef158934564-ringed-deriv.reading_limits: Read the stated localization definition, stability definition and exactness discussion with Proposition 1.1.4.1 and its proof, the differential graded nerve construction and functoriality discussion, Definition 1.3.2.1, Remark 1.3.2.2 and the cone square of Remark 1.3.2.17 on 2026-11-12. thm-adjudicate-1ef158934564-ringed-deriv.title: Jacob Lurie, Higher Topos Theory: higher categorical formulation and preservation of colimits

thm-adjudicate-1ef158934564-ringed-deriv.statement: Infinity-categories are simplicial sets with inner horn fillers; ordinary categories enter by their nerves. The homotopy category has vertices as objects and homotopy classes of edges as arrows. Fun(C,E) is the simplicial mapping object; its edges are natural transformations. Presentable means accessible and admitting small colimits. Accessibility means generation under small kappa-filtered colimits by an essentially small collection of kappa-compact objects, for some regular kappa. Left adjoints preserve all existing colimits.
thm-adjudicate-1ef158934564-ringed-deriv.hypotheses: The specified infinity-categories, with smallness, colimits and accessibility measured in the chosen base universe; the functor categories are formed in a larger universe. For colimit preservation, a functor admitting a right adjoint.

thm-adjudicate-9ead0798f06a-projective-q.title: Charles Weibel, The K-book, author-hosted standalone Chapter IV
thm-adjudicate-9ead0798f06a-projective-q.statement: The nerve/classifying-space, Q and Waldhausen S constructions define full K-spaces. Exact-category S/Q is a natural equivalence compatible with object maps. For split exact categories Q agrees with direct-sum group completion; for finite free modules its stabilized automorphism map is the acyclic plus map. The projective version has components K_0(R).
thm-adjudicate-9ead0798f06a-projective-q.hypotheses: Use small presentations of essentially small exact or Waldhausen categories in fixed universes; split exactness for group-completion/Q. thm-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-oriented-fie.statement: The actual graded comparison is induced by the augmented multiplicative filtered K→KH map. On smooth prime-field schemes its classical composite is the canonical Kan-extension/cdh comparison. The actual EM Picard map is defined from (4.9) by the Nisnevich-local left-Kan construction. Lemma 5.12 identifies the actual graded image of 1-[O(-1)] with the first Chern class of O(1), under the classical-to-EM comparison. Theorems 4.10(1) and 4.24(1) supply the motivic negative-weight vanishing. Theorem 3.5(1), with §2.2, supplies zero negative graded pieces of the cdh KH-filtration. The proof of Theorem 4.10 explicitly uses the convention Z(j)_cdh(X)=0 for j<0. In the item, these negative cdh coefficients mean precisely gr^j_cdh KH(X)[-2j], and the negative component of the same structured filtered comparison is the canonical zero-to-zero equivalence. This is the stated zero-extension convention; Theorem 6.1 itself is invoked only for nonnegative weights.
thm-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-oriented-fie.hypotheses: The functors and filtered comparison are on all qcqs schemes over a prime field F. Construction 4.36 and Theorem 6.1(2) state the coefficient comparison and regular-Noetherian equivalence for j≥0; the latter includes smooth finite-type schemes over every extension field of F. For every qcqs Q-scheme, Theorem 4.10(1) gives zero motivic coefficients for j<0; Theorem 4.24(1) gives the same for every qcqs F_p-scheme. The cdh filtration in Theorem 3.5(1) is N-indexed on every qcqs F-scheme, with no finite-dimensional or regularity condition for that assertion. Its finite-valuative-dimension clause concerns boundedness only. Section 2.2 defines N-indexing as constancy at the augmented underlying object in filtration degrees j≤0, equivalently exhaustiveness and zero negative graded pieces.

thm-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-oriented-fie.statement: The unit induces canonical E∞ zero-slice equivalences. The structured graded coefficients retain products and the unit-adjoint P¹ class. In the proof of Lemma 3.27, restriction along O(1) identifies homotopy classes of maps Σ∞Pic→F¹ with reduced π₀F¹(P¹_X): PBF and zero negative weights make the tower constant from m=1 and kill lim¹. This proves homotopy of (3.28); the lemma’s final statement only asserts agreement on units. The canonical cdh→represented comparison and field restriction are multiplicative, and the determinant/edge square specifies the Picard map. The imported framework is the stable symmetric monoidal motivic infinity-category SH(X), its motivic sphere, Tate twist, effective covers and cofiber slices; multiplicative filtered and graded objects use Day convolution. Picard denotes the line-bundle groupoid with trivial-line base point. Nisnevich and cdh sheafification and smooth left Kan extension have the conventions of Definition 2.5 and Proposition 2.23. The KGL orientation uses the Bott element defined by 1-[O(-1)] on the reduced projective line. On qcqs schemes over a field, Corollary 8.16 makes the canonical A¹-localization of cdh coefficients an equivalence. Theorem 9.1 identifies that localization with the base-changed theory Z(j)^(A,cdh), through the canonical comparison of (7.14); Theorem 9.3(2) identifies its subsequent map (4.19) to Z(j)^A as an equivalence of graded E∞ algebras. Hence their specified composite is an equivalence on qcqs schemes over any field in every integer weight.
thm-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-oriented-fie.hypotheses: Structured coefficient constructions on qcqs schemes; Lemma3.27 requires A¹-local Nisnevich graded ring theory, zero negative weights and PBF; Construction4.35 on regular Noetherian bases, extended by Theorem4.39(4). Field base-independence for every field. For the equal-characteristic comparison, Corollary 8.16 is applied to a qcqs scheme X over an arbitrary field and any integer weight j. Neither perfectness nor a finite-type or dimension bound is required there. Theorems 9.1 and 9.3 apply to every qcqs scheme and every integer weight, integrally. For the Picard detector, X is qcqs and the two spectral Chern maps have domain RΓ_Nis(-,G_m)[1] on Sm_X. Their O(1) classes on P¹_X agree in π₀; PBF is an equivalence of spectra relative to the first map. The item uses the proof’s reduced-suspension mapping assertion, before the lemma’s conclusion on units.

lem-adjudicate-37c8a46c3b6b-open-natural.statement: HSpt(C) is the localization of strict sequential simplicial spectral presheaves at pointwise stable weak equivalences. Corollary 4.1.5 identifies the rectified K-theory layer Q_j with the raw layer on smooth morphisms in HSpt. The first sentence of the proof of Theorem 6.5.1 explicitly states Z^j ≅ K^(j/j+1) in HSpt(k), before deriving the theorem about its layers. Theorem 5.3.1(3) and Theorem 6.4.2 compare the raw layer through its iterated layer with the ordinary simplicial cycle spectrum: the latter proof uses the canonical zeroth Postnikov map and checks the cycle face maps. These constructions give the pointwise open-restriction chain used here. Section 6.5 by itself also states a Nisnevich-derived comparison, from which no pointwise conclusion is inferred. Example 8.2.2(3) assembles the ordinary classical spectrum, Remark 8.3.1 supplies strict lifts, and Theorem 9.0.3 with Remark 9.0.4 identifies the stable coniveau and slice towers over perfect fields. Sections 10.4–10.5 identify the classical zeroth slice. Only the fixed-weight underlying spectrum comparison and its positive ordinary coefficient are used. Section 6.5 defines Z^j as the ordinary Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectral presheaf of its fibrant complex. Example 8.2.2(3) and §10.4 assemble these same entries into Z. Sections 8.1–8.2 give tail suspension and the derived zeroth-entry adjunction, with pointwise comparison of entries between fibrant models (Remark 8.2.1(2)). Section 1.6 makes Postnikov constructions functorial on diagrams. Sections 2.1–2.2 give support and layer functoriality for open restrictions. Theorem 6.4.1 and the proof of Theorem 6.4.2 supply the supported coherent-sheaf G-theory maps and the positive structure-sheaf generator used in the local restriction-square argument. The proof of Theorem 6.4.1 imports the regular-ambient resolution comparison K(S) to G(S) and the supported localization equivalence K^Z(S) with G(Z). The localization leg is G(Z) to fib(G(S) to G(S minus Z)); the resolution comparisons on the regular ambient and its open complement identify this fiber with K^Z(S). The proof of Theorem 6.4.2 uses that same supported map from G(Z) to the iterated coniveau layer. The explicit open-pair fiber zigzag and its natural inverse in this item are local applications of those imported comparisons, not additional theorems attributed to the source.
lem-adjudicate-37c8a46c3b6b-open-natural.hypotheses: Smooth separated finite-type schemes; fixed perfect base k for the stable slice comparison. Use the global presheaf models and ordinary cycle realization. No use of the conditional module assertion in Corollary 10.5.2 or Conjecture 11.1.1. K in this auxiliary calculation is Levine's chosen presheaf; no separate identification with the EM perfect-complex model is a premise.
